title: Virion structure
caption: A virion has a genome of DNA or RNA inside a protein coat, the capsid, which is made of capsomeres. Some viruses also have a lipid envelope from the host membrane, with glycoproteins that stick out of it. A virus has no cell, no ribosomes and no metabolism. Typical sizes are 20–300 nm; the drawing is not to scale.
alt: Two virions. A non-enveloped one: a hexagonal capsid enclosing a coiled genome. An enveloped one: a round lipid envelope with spikes of glycoprotein, enclosing a capsid and a coiled genome.
description: Genome of DNA or RNA, single- or double-stranded.
A protein capsid made of capsomeres.
Some viruses have a lipid envelope from the host membrane, with glycoproteins.
No cell, ribosomes or metabolism: viruses replicate only inside host cells.
